claims.text: Deep cryogenic treatment of as-printed AlCrFeNiSi miniature components will relieve residual thermal stresses.
Deep cryogenic treatment will improve the mechanical properties of additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
A DCT-induced phase transition contributes to improved strength and ductility.
DCT-induced dislocation rearrangement improves mechanical properties.
Conventionally L-PBF-fabricated AlCrFeNiSi parts exhibit high residual thermal stresses.
Conventionally L-PBF-fabricated AlCrFeNiSi parts exhibit degraded yield strength and ductility.
Conventionally L-PBF-fabricated AlCrFeNiSi parts have complex, non-optimized microstructures.
The proposed treatment consists of liquid-nitrogen immersion at approximately -196 °C for 12 hours followed by controlled warming.
The proposed treatment window applies to components with features on the 1–10 mm scale.
DCT will produce recrystallized grain refinement in AlCrFeNiSi.
DCT will reorder dislocations in AlCrFeNiSi.
DCT may form nanoscale precipitates that relax internal stresses.
Phase adjustment and dislocation reorganization release stored thermal stresses.
DCT-treated AlCrFeNiSi parts will have statistically lower XRD-measured residual stress than untreated parts.
DCT-treated AlCrFeNiSi parts will have higher yield strength than untreated parts.
DCT-treated AlCrFeNiSi parts will have higher ultimate tensile strength than untreated parts.
DCT-treated AlCrFeNiSi parts will have greater elongation than untreated parts.
Rapid solidification during conventional high-thermal-input L-PBF causes retained residual stresses and an unfavorable microstructural state.
DCT has produced strength and elongation improvements and an induced phase transition in another additively manufactured high-entropy alloy.
Failure to obtain statistically significant residual-stress reduction and tensile-property improvements relative to an untreated control will falsify the hypothesis.
